meaning.zh:
“与邻居攀比” 或 “与人斗富”。

这个成语起源于20世纪初的美国，特别是1913年漫画家阿瑟·R·“匹浦”·李斯（Arthur R. "Pop" Momand）创作的连环漫画《与琼斯家攀比》（Keeping Up with the Joneses）。漫画描绘了一家人不断努力与他们邻居 “琼斯家” 在外在物质上相媲美。这个短语后来常用来描述人们企图通过购买豪华物品和展示财富去追赶或超越他人的行为。
meaning.en: This idiom originates from early 20th-century America, particularly from a comic strip created by Arthur R. "Pop" Momand in 1913 titled "Keeping Up with the Joneses." The comic depicted a family constantly striving to keep up with their neighbors, the Joneses, in terms of material possessions. The phrase later came to be used to describe the behavior of individuals attempting to match or surpass others in wealth and social status by purchasing luxury items.

lines.en: They're always *keeping up with the Joneses*, trying to buy every new gadget their neighbors get.
lines.zh: 他们总是与邻居攀比，试图买下邻居买的每一个新玩意儿。

lines.en: She spent a lot of money on that car just to *keep up with the Joneses*.
lines.zh: 她花了很多钱买那辆车，只是为了和邻居攀比。

lines.en: Don't stress about *keeping up with the Joneses*; just live within your means.
lines.zh: 不要为与人攀比而感到压力；量入为出，过好自己的生活。
